subject: On-prem deployment: license carve-outs & evidence-handback coordination
messages:
From: Tina Lopez <t.lopez@medivex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anil Sharma <anil.sharma@medivex.com>, procurement@medivex.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: on-prem license carve-outs + evidence flow (MSA redlines attached)

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal pushed back on a few items in the MSA and the Order Form related to our on-prem (air-gapped) deployment. Please see attached redlines (Medivex_MSA_redlines_v1.docx) and an annotated Order Form. High level asks:

- We need explicit language confirming the narrow license scope for the deployed runtime (no resale / no external hosting).
- Operator access: Medivex requires that Redwood provide an "operator witness" model for initial evidence validation (30-day window after go-live) rather than continuous operator access.
- Snapshot deposit / escrow-like pathway: we want an option that allows Medivex to request a sealed but verifiable runtime snapshot and a witness session with Redwood engineers.
- Audit window: allow two annual audit windows limited to forensics and license compliance, with remote witnessing preferred.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept these carve-outs or propose alternate language? Procurement also requested a simple evidence matrix (who/what/when) so they can map the order form exhibits.

Cc'ing Anil (counsel) — happy to set a 30-minute legal sync.

Best,
Tina
Procurement Lead, Medivex

Attachments: Medivex_MSA_redlines_v1.docx, OrderForm-Draft-annotated.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <t.lopez@medivex.com>
Cc: Anil Sharma <anil.sharma@medivex.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: on-prem license carve-outs + evidence flow (MSA redlines attached)

Tina —

Appreciate the clear asks and the annotated doc. Quick answers up front:

- License scope: YES, we can accept narrow runtime residency and a no-resale clause; we will map that into the MSA + Order Form exhibits.
- Operator witness instead of continuous operator access: reasonable for initial validation and for major upgrades; we need to align on the definition and timing (we typically do a 2-week witness window during which we provide encrypted snapshot access and a Zoom witness session).
- Snapshot deposit: we can offer a sealed snapshot deposit model (cryptographic hash + witness) as an Order Form exhibit; there are operational and KMS implications we should run through.
- Audit windows: two limited remote audit windows per year is workable, with agreed scoping and an evidence requester workflow.

Next steps I propose: 1) internal legal review to propose clean redlines, 2) produce an evidence_matrix_template and a short runbook for the witness workflow, 3) 30-min call with Anil to walk through the proposed language.

Marissa — can you prepare the evidence matrix template and a short draft runbook for the witness session?

Cc'ing Anil so we can calendar a legal sync.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0172

Subject: Internal: Medivex MSA redlines — legal help + runbook/ops ask

Team —

Forwarding Medivex redlines (attached above). Highlights for legal:
- They want explicit language limiting license to runtime used only by Medivex and forbidding any external hosting or sublicensing. Please propose explicit Order Form exhibit language and a short definition for "licensed runtime".
- Operator access: they prefer an "operator witness" approach. We need to decide parameters: witness window length, what telemetry/log access we provision, acceptance criteria.
- Snapshot deposit: they asked for an escrow-like pathway that is sealed and verifiable — operationally this looks like: create a snapshot tarball, compute SHA256, deposit hash to a mutually accessible ledger (we can use DocuSign timestamp or signed statement), and make snapshot available for a time-limited witness session. Need legal/infra thoughts on liability and retention.
- Audit windows: two remote windows per year, limited scope; legal needs to propose constraints (SLA for scheduling, confidentiality, data minimization).

Marissa — action: create evidence_matrix_template.xlsx listing artifact, owner, retention, and witness procedure. Goal: 24 hours.
Laura — action: propose clean redline suggestions for the MSA license paragraph and an Order Form exhibit for the snapshot/witness option. Also flag any risk language we should push back on (e.g., open-ended retention or indemnity carveouts).
Priyom — please prep a short summary for the customer call (talking points + trade-offs).

Target: respond to Medivex with proposed clean redlines and the evidence matrix by EOD tomorrow so we can keep procurement momentum.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Medivex MSA redlines — legal help + runbook/ops ask

Thanks Ben — quick legal read and plan below. I've attached a short redline digest (we will push clean redlines to the doc this afternoon). High-level positions:

1) License scope: propose this clause: "Customer is granted a non-transferable, non-sublicensable, perpetual (for the term of the Order Form) license to use the runtime solely for Customer internal use in Customer-controlled infrastructure. Provider expressly disclaims any right to host, resell, or otherwise make the runtime available to third parties on Customer's behalf." This limits exposure and is narrow enough for procurement.

2) Operator witness & snapshot: propose we offer an optional Order Form exhibit titled "Witnessed Snapshot Exhibit" that defines: snapshot creation, cryptographic hash process, time-limited witness session (max 14 days after request), and a limitation of Redwood liability to acts of gross negligence in the witness process. Also require Customer to provide a runbook of the steps they wish validated.

3) Audit windows: propose two remote audit windows per 12 months, each limited to a defined evidence scope and requiring 30 days notice and a mutually agreed scheduling window. Add confidentiality and data minimization obligations for auditors.

4) Retention & custody: do not agree to deposit full keys or live secrets. The snapshot should exclude unencrypted customer data unless Customer requests a forensics snapshot under a separate exhibit with defined controls.

5) DocuSign / formalities: suggest we include the sealed-hash timestamp via DocuSign or Azure Timestamp as the evidentiary mechanism and include a short appendix on KMS responsibilities.

Operational asks for Marissa/Infra: we'll need a short operations statement outlining how we will produce snapshot artifacts, what logs we can reasonably provide, and the witness playbook. Keep it high level in the exhibit and move detailed runbook to a separate SOP referenced by the exhibit.

I'll prepare the clean MSA/Order Form redlines and the Witnessed Snapshot Exhibit today and share links. If Priyom can run the 30-min customer legal sync with Ben and Anil at 3pm PT, we can walk them through the proposed language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: redline_digest.pdf (summary)
